The claim is incorrect — on an incline, the normal force only balances the *perpendicular* component of weight ($F_N=mg\cos\theta$), which is less than the full weight for any nonzero incline angle; only on a flat (horizontal, $\theta=0^\circ$) surface does the normal force equal the full weight.
The claim is correct, but only for inclines steeper than $45^\circ$.
The claim is incorrect, because the normal force is always zero on an incline.

incorrect.3: The normal force is not zero (unless the incline is vertical, $\theta=90^\circ$); it takes on the value $mg\cos\theta$, which is nonzero for any incline angle less than $90^\circ$.
